title: Worksheet — A Bottle of Dew (Class 6 CBSE English)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions. Show working / write full sentences for the subjective questions. Total time: 30 minutes.

questions.question: Who brings a drop of dew on a leaf to the king?
questions.explanation: The child's offering wins the king's approval.

questions.question: What is the moral of the story?
options: Gold is the most valuable thing.
The present moment is the most precious thing.
questions.answer: The present moment is the most precious thing.

questions.question: Retell the story in 4-5 sentences in your own words.
questions.answer: A wise old king gathers his people and asks them to bring the most precious thing in the world to fill his crystal bottle. A goldsmith brings gold, a poet brings written words, a farmer brings a grain of rice. A child brings a leaf with a single drop of morning dew. The king accepts the dew because it represents the present moment, which cannot be stored. He keeps the bottle as a daily reminder to be thankful.
questions.explanation: A correct retelling captures characters, four offerings, and the moral.

questions.question: Why is 'a drop of dew' a perfect symbol of the present moment?
questions.answer: A dew drop forms in the early morning, sparkles briefly, and then evaporates. It cannot be stored or saved. Just as the present moment cannot be repeated, the dew cannot be brought back once it has gone — so dew is a perfect symbol of NOW.
questions.explanation: Dew is brief and unique to its moment.

questions.question: Underline the COMMON nouns in this sentence: 'The wise king listened to the goldsmith, the poet and the child in the courtyard.' Then list them.
questions.answer: Common nouns: king, goldsmith, poet, child, courtyard. (No proper nouns; all roles are described in general terms.)
questions.explanation: Common nouns name a class of people / places / things.

questions.question: Convert each sentence to PAST TENSE: (i) The king holds the bottle. (ii) The child smiles at the king. (iii) The villagers walk to the courtyard.
questions.answer: (i) The king HELD the bottle. (ii) The child SMILED at the king. (iii) The villagers WALKED to the courtyard.
questions.explanation: hold → held (irregular); smile → smiled and walk → walked (regular).

questions.question: If YOU were one of the king's subjects, what would you bring as the most precious thing in the world? Explain in 5-6 sentences. Use at least two adjectives and at least one past-tense verb.
questions.answer: Sample answer: 'I would bring a hand-written letter from my best friend. Friendship is precious because it cannot be bought. A friend who knows me, who listened to my secrets, who laughed at my silly jokes — that is something neither gold nor rice can match. The letter holds her words, and her words hold our friendship. I would tie a small ribbon around it and place it gently in the king's bottle. Even the king, I think, would smile at this.' (Open-ended; rubric: clear choice + reason + adjectives + past-tense verb.)
questions.explanation: Encourages original thinking aligned with the story's theme.

questions.question: Write a paragraph (5-6 sentences) describing a precious MOMENT (not an object) from your own life. Use 'precious' and 'thankful' in your paragraph.
questions.answer: Sample: 'Last winter my grandmother came to visit. One quiet morning, she and I walked to the garden together. The dew was still on the grass and sparkling in the sun. We didn't speak much; she just held my hand. That walk was precious to me. I am thankful for that moment, because I know it cannot return.' (Rubric: clear moment, both vocabulary words used, 5-6 sentences, past tense.)
questions.explanation: Connects story's moral to student's real life.
